next_step: Use one worker-unit to calibrate that changing observation clocks leaves the physical kinetics unchanged and readout noninvasive. Use the other to measure endpoint probabilities and projected reaction activity under multiple calibrated clocks from the same preparation; compare the joint data with the shared-clock hierarchy and the one-clock fit.
decisive_observation: Whether calibrated multi-clock data violate a finite-level outer constraint of the shared-clock hierarchy, or merely remain compatible with it.
outcome_decisions: If data violate a constraint, check calibration and assumptions; if they hold, investigate clock-dependent kinetics or limits of the representation.
If data are compatible, retain the hierarchy as a useful constraint, then seek higher-level bounds or a conditional completeness proof; compatibility alone does not identify the physical generator.
retained_result: Keep the proved one-clock characterization and its occupation-weighted interpretation for its stated entrance and observation clock. Do not treat its fitted generator as the physical generator; the binary example already shows clock-dependent mismatch.
uncertainty: No finite convergence rate is available, and compatibility at finite levels may be weak. Negative evidence is scoped to calibrated clocks and the hierarchy assumptions; it does not rule out arbitrary interventions or mechanisms outside those assumptions.
